mentions.name: Framework for persistent complex systems
mentions.description: A scientific framework defining what makes complex systems persist, combining information theory, thermodynamics, and control theory. It yields six pillars that all persistent systems must have, a fundamental 'Action' such systems take, and three rules for how persistent systems must subdivide. The framework is applied to domains including religion, language, AI models, business, the cell, quantum physics, and number theory, and is being applied to LLMs as token streams that persist, enabling mapping unsolved problems in one domain to solved ones in another.
mentions.problem: Understanding why complex systems fail or persist, such as companies failing, Rome collapsing, or why people age and die.
mentions.source_excerpt:
Developing a rigorous scientific definition of what make complex systems persist.

The opposite of the favorite questions: Why did that company I worked for fail? Why did Rome collapse? Why do people get old and die?

Combining information theory with thermodynamics and control theory you get:
1) A set of six pillars that all systems that persist must have.
2) A fundamental 'Action' that all of these systems take. 
3) A set of three rules for how system that persists must subdivide
